create.name: Vedanta Society of New York
create.bio:
The Vedanta Society of New York is the oldest Vedanta centre in the West and the first centre of the Ramakrishna Order anywhere. Swami Vivekananda started it in 1894, the year after his celebrated addresses at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago, when a group of American students began meeting with him in a couple of rented rooms in Manhattan. After several moves it settled in 1921 in the house on West 71st Street that it still occupies, and a line of monks of the Order has led it ever since.

Its teaching follows Vedanta as lived and explained by Sri Ramakrishna and Vivekananda: that every person is at heart divine, that the world's religions are different roads to the same truth, and that each seeker may follow the yoga of knowledge, devotion, work or meditation that suits them. Since 2017 its resident minister has been Swami Sarvapriyananda, whose talks on Advaita Vedanta reach a very large audience online. Sunday morning lectures, weekday classes on the Bhagavad Gita and the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna, evening vespers with meditation and festival worship take place at the society, and most talks are streamed and archived on YouTube.

free_resources.title: Upcoming Events
free_resources.description: The society's regular programme in Manhattan, mostly livestreamed: an hour-long Sunday lecture, usually by the resident minister, weekday classes reading the Bhagavad Gita and the Gospel of Sri Ramakrishna with time for questions, evening arati with meditation, and festival worship.

free_resources.title: Introductory Lectures
free_resources.description: A starting set of recorded talks for newcomers on the four yogas, Advaita Vedanta, practical Vedanta and the harmony of religions, each with a short introduction to the theme.
